subject: Continuity runbook: exception request for multi-region failover
messages:
From: Erik Johansen <erik.johansen@nordicbank.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: NordicBank Security <security@nordicbank.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:15:00 +0100
Subject: Multi-region failover commitments / request for exception

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week. We reviewed Redwood's standard regional failover SLAs with our SRE and security teams and we'd like to request an exception for cross-border (EU -> non-EU) failover behavior. Brief summary of our ask:

- During a region-wide outage that requires intercontinental failover (EU -> US), NordicBank needs an explicit documented RTO and RPO.
- We understand Redwood's hosted SLA targets 99.95% and 5-minute cold-start RTO within a single region, but cross-border failover will have additional constraints (DNS, cache warming, KV replication).
- For contractual purposes, we'd like to propose an interim SLA amendment allowing up to 45 minute RTO and up to 15 minute RPO for intercontinental failover for a pilot period, with required operational runbook and a quarterly drill.

Attached is our internal continuity runbook excerpt highlighting timing expectations and our compliance team's checklist (attachment: nordicbank-initial-failover-req.pdf).

Can Redwood confirm whether an exception like this is feasible from an operational and contractual standpoint and outline the technical mitigations you would apply?

Goal: get a written proposal that we can circulate with procurement/legal and then proceed to a signature/technical kickoff.

Best,
Erik

Erik Johansen
Head of Platform Resilience
NordicBank
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Erik Johansen <erik.johansen@nordicbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Multi-region failover commitments / request for exception

Hi Erik — thanks for the clear ask and the runbook excerpt. I appreciate the context (and the compliance checklist). We're happy to evaluate and propose a scoped amendment.

Short answers up-front:
- Feasible: Yes, we can document an exception path for intercontinental failover with explicit RTO/RPO bounds, but it will require operational constraints and a limited-scope addendum to our hosted SLA.
- Trade-offs: Longer RTO/RPO, pre-warming costs, and certain model/feature restrictions (KV-prefill required; tooling such as streaming may be limited during active failover).

Next steps I'd like to propose:
1) Internal technical assessment (I will loop in Marcus and Laura) — confirm realistic RTO/RPO targets by deployment type (hosted vs dedicated) and list mitigations.
2) Draft an SLA amendment + runbook that specifies the failover sequence, responsibilities, and drill cadence.
3) Legal/procurement review and signature via DocuSign.

Can you confirm the scope: is this for production only or also for non-prod? Also, is data residency a hard blocker for replication to a US region, or is the requirement limited to live failover only (i.e., data-at-rest must remain in EU unless invoked)?

I've attached a short checklist we use when assessing failover requests (redwood-failover-checklist.xlsx). Marcus/Laura/Hannah — can you pick this up and come back with a proposed technical plan and a cost delta?

Thanks,
Olga

Olga Petrov
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:30:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region failover commitments / request for exception

Olga / Laura — quick technical assessment below (high level) based on current Redwood runtime behavior and the specifics from Erik's runbook.

Summary findings:
- Single-region failover (within EU): we can meet 5–10 minute RTO for most configurations if KV cache warmup is enabled and autoscaling is configured to pre-warm based on flagged health checks. RPO ~ <1 minute with async replication enabled.
- Intercontinental failover (EU->US): realistic RTO range is 30–60 minutes depending on workload characteristics (sequence length, embedding/LLM cache state). RPO depends on replication window; with continuous replication we can target 10–15 minutes, otherwise 30+ minutes.

Recommended approach for a 45-minute RTO / 15-minute RPO concession (what we'd propose):
- Architecture: warm-standby active in US region with async KV replication from EU primary. Traffic cutover via weighted routing + fast DNS TTL (30s) + healthcheck probe-based failover.
- Operational steps: pre-warm models and KV caches on standby nightly for a 1-hour window prior to high-risk periods; maintain a rolling cache snapshot cadence.
- Constraints: during failover we will cap max concurrency per customer to avoid oversubscription; streaming SSE and long-lived function calls may be limited until KV rebuild finishes.
- Cost impact: warm-standby adds a baseline of ~1.4x hosted compute cost for reserved capacity; additional egress and replication fees apply.

Attachments: warm-standby-cost-estimate.csv (cost scenarios), and a short checklist for the playbook.

Open items for legal/procurement:
- Need a time-bound amendment (pilot for 3 months) and explicit rollback terms if capacity or behavior deviates.
- Define SLAs by failure class (regional outage vs provider-wide incident).

If you want, we can prepare two variants: (A) 45m RTO / 15m RPO pilot (recommended), (B) 60m RTO / 30m RPO lower-cost option.

I'll assemble a short runbook and mark the required changes in the SLA doc.

Thanks,
Marcus

Marcus Lin
Sr. Product Manager, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Erik Johansen <erik.johansen@nordicbank.com>
Cc: Helena Larsson <helena.larsson@nordicbank.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, NordicBank Security <security@nordicbank.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 10:02:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Multi-region failover commitments / request for exception

Erik / Helena — thanks for your patience while we assessed the operational and contractual implications. Below is a concise proposal we can take to procurement/legal and then finalize with a technical kickoff.

Proposal (summary):
- Scope: Production systems only (non-prod excluded).
- Duration: 3-month pilot beginning on signature.
- SLA amendment: Intercontinental failover (EU -> non-EU) RTO cap: 45 minutes; RPO cap: 15 minutes. This applies when the documented runbook is followed and pre-failover warm-up procedures are executed.
- Operational requirements (NordicBank responsibilities): maintain health-check endpoints for routing, participate in quarterly drills, provide an approved incident commander contact list, and authorize temporary cross-border replication in failover scenarios.
- Redwood responsibilities: maintain warm-standby capacity per the agreed configuration, perform nightly KV snapshot rotations, execute failover playbook, and provide post-drill run reports.
- Limitations: Streaming and certain long-lived connections may be curtailed during active failover; model feature parity will be noted in the amendment.
- Cost: estimated delta as discussed (warm-standby baseline ~1.4x compute); detailed cost sheet attached.

Next steps:
1) Confirm scope: please reply if production-only pilot is acceptable and whether data residency permissions for temporary replication are approved.
2) Upon confirmation, we'll issue SLA amendment draft (redwood-nordicbank-sla-amendment-v1.docx) and a failover runbook (failover-playbook-v1.pdf) for legal review.
3) Sign via DocuSign (link provided) and schedule a technical kickoff and first drill within 30 days of signature.

DocuSign preview: https://docusign.com/txn/ABC1234
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/84722/NB-34712
Confluence runbook (internal): https://docs.redwood.com/confluence/display/OPS/NordicBank+Failover+Runbook

If you want a lower-cost alternative (60m RTO / 30m RPO) we can include that as an appendix; Marcus included two clear cost/availability trade-offs in his note.

Please let us know if you'd like a short (30m) technical walkthrough this week to go over the failover sequence.

Best regards,
Olga

Olga Petrov
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-nordicbank-sla-amendment-v1.docx; failover-playbook-v1.pdf
